subject: paper:wolraich-1995
quote: The meta-analytic synthesis of the studies to date found that sugar does not affect the behavior or cognitive performance of children.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The core finding across 23 blinded placebo-controlled studies — no behavioural or cognitive effect of sugar.

subject: paper:wolraich-1995
quote: The strong belief of parents may be due to expectancy and common association.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Attributes the entrenched belief to expectancy and coincidence rather than a real effect.

subject: paper:nigg-2012
quote: Restriction diets reduced ADHD symptoms at an effect of g = 0.29 (95% CI, 0.07-0.53).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. A small-to-moderate meta-analytic effect for restriction diets, with the conclusion that they benefit some children.

subject: paper:nigg-2012
quote: For food colors, parent reports yielded an effect size of g = 0.18 (95% CI, 0.08-0.24; p = .0007), which decreased to 0.12 (95% CI, 0.01-0.23; p < .05) after adjustment for possible publication bias.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Food-color effects are small and shrink further after correcting for publication bias — the honest small print.

subject: paper:bloch-2011
quote: Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation, particularly with higher doses of eicosapentaenoic acid, was modestly effective in the treatment of ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Omega-3 is modestly effective and, per the same abstract, less so than standard pharmacotherapy.
